transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My doctor asked me to come in because she’s concerned my eating has gotten too restricted. I guess my meal planning is pretty tight, but to me it feels orderly—like yogurt for breakfast, maybe skipping lunch if I’m busy, and then a very measured dinner so the day stays controlled.
Are you worried about gaining weight if you don't follow your current eating plan?

Yes. If the scale is up even a pound after I’ve had a normal dinner, or eaten at a restaurant, I get this sharp panic feeling. It feels like I’ve lost control, and then I feel like I have to correct it the next day.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Yes, I have lost some. My weight has drifted down more than my doctor is comfortable with. I know that’s part of why she sent me here. But honestly, when I look at the number, I still catch myself thinking it would feel better if it were just a little lower—more manageable somehow.
Do you feel like you would lose control if you didn't stick to your meal plan?

Yes. That’s pretty much what it feels like. If I eat outside the plan—like a normal dinner or at a restaurant—and the scale is even up a pound after, I get really panicky. It feels like I’ve lost control, and then I feel like I need to make up for it the next day.
Do you think your weight is currently at a healthy level?

Honestly, I don’t always see it the way my doctor does. She’s said it’s getting medically unsafe, but part of me thinks she may be overstating it because I’m still working, doing my errands, taking care of my own life. So… I know she’s concerned, but it doesn’t always feel unhealthy to me.
Do you think you look overweight now?

I don’t know if I’d say I look overweight exactly. But I do notice my waist and hips a lot. If my clothes feel like they contain them neatly, I feel like I’m doing okay. If they don’t, then I start feeling like I’ve let myself go.
Do you think your weight or body shape is the main thing that determines your self-worth?

I think… more than I’d like to admit, yes. I know I’m an older woman, and I’m not trying to look young or anything. But I do judge how well I’m handling myself by whether my waist and hips look contained in my clothes. If they do, I feel more okay about myself. If they don’t, it really affects how I see myself.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you restrict your food intake?

Yes, I think it is. If the scale is up even a pound after I’ve had a normal dinner or gone out to a restaurant, I get this sharp panic, like I’ve lost control. Then I feel like I have to make up for it the next day by cutting back.
Have you experienced any significant medical problems as a result of your weight loss?
Not that I’m aware of. I mean, I haven’t had anything I’d call a significant medical problem from it. If there’s something specific you mean, I’m not sure, but nothing major has stood out to me.
Do you ever eat an amount of food that you consider excessive in a short period of time?
Not really. I don’t think I usually eat what I’d call an excessive amount in a short time. If anything, I’m usually watching the amount pretty closely.
Do you ever feel like you've eaten an excessive amount of food in a short period of time?
I don’t think so. Sometimes it feels like I ate too much, but when I look at it plainly, it’s not really a large amount in a short time. It’s more that I’m uncomfortable with it.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No, I don’t make myself vomit after eating.
Do you ever feel like you've eaten an amount of food that you couldn't stop or control?
I’m not sure I’d say I couldn’t stop or control it. I haven’t really noticed that happening. It’s more that I’m careful about what I’m eating.
Do you ever use laxatives or diuretics to try to lose weight or prevent weight gain?
No, I don’t use laxatives or diuretics for that.
Have you had your menstrual period in the past three months?
I’m not sure how to answer that at my age. I don’t really have menstrual periods anymore.
Do you think you would be extremely upset if you gained a small amount of weight, even if it was still within a healthy range?

Yes. Even a pound or so can really upset me. If I see the scale go up after a normal dinner or eating out, I feel this sudden panic, like I’ve lost control, and then I feel like I need to make up for it the next day.
Do you ever feel like you've eaten an amount of food that's much larger than most people would eat in a short period of time?
I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes I feel like I ate too much, but I wouldn’t say it’s an amount much larger than what most people would eat in a short time.
Do you ever feel like you've eaten an amount of food that's much, much larger than what you would normally eat in a short period of time?
Not really, no. I might feel like I ate more than I should have, but not much, much larger than what I’d normally eat in a short period.
Do you ever feel like you've eaten in a way that felt out of control?
I’m not sure I’d call it out of control. I can feel upset or uncomfortable after eating, but I don’t usually feel like I can’t stop myself once I’ve started.
Do you ever feel like you've eaten in a way that felt out of control to the point where you consumed a large amount of food?
No, I don’t think so. I might feel bad about what I ate, but I don’t think I’ve eaten a large amount in a way where I felt out of control.
